Per-patient shift for exponentiating log densities

Source: R/dynamicPredictionShared.R
patient_log_shift.Rd

The conditional-density helpers (conditionalYT() and relatives) return log densities, one column per patient. Every quantity a prediction needs is a ratio of sums of those densities within one patient, so any per-patient constant cancels: this returns, for each patient, the largest finite log density across all the matrices given, to subtract before exponentiating (see exp_shifted()). Without it the densities – whose scale is the determinant of a covariance matrix that grows with the number of observations and with the biomarkers' units – underflowed to 0 or overflowed to Inf.

Usage

patient_log_shift(...)

Arguments

...

Matrices of log densities, rows = grid points, columns = patients (all with the same columns).

Value

A numeric vector, one shift per patient (0 for a patient with no finite value).
